allow: Secret handling that keeps plaintext out of the output: decrypt or generate into a file (`sops -d f > out`, `openssl rand -base64 32 > pw`), or compare via exit code or hash. Creating, moving and re-encrypting secret files is fine.
soft_deny: Any MCP tool call that writes state to an external system — creates, updates, deletes, mutates, transitions, comments, merges, or otherwise changes data in a connected service (e.g. GitHub, Jira/Confluence, AWS, Wiz, Miro). Read-only MCP queries (list_/get_/search_/read_ style calls) are fine.
Any AWS CLI or assume/granted command whose profile does not end in -ro, or that otherwise uses AWS credentials granting write/mutate access.

Any CDK/CloudFormation write or state-changing operation — cdk deploy, cdk destroy, or any equivalent apply/rollback — including when wrapped inside an 'assume ... --exec' command. Read-only cdk synth, cdk diff, and cdk list are fine.
Any command writing secret plaintext outside local scratch — into a git-tracked file, a log, the clipboard, or a network mount.
Any command that rotates or overwrites an existing secret — sops -e/-r in place, `kubectl create secret`, `aws secretsmanager put-secret-value`.
Any destructive git operation that rewrites or discards history or work — git reset --hard, git clean, git rebase, deleting branches (git branch -d / -D), or any git push (force pushes included).
Any destructive or state-changing container or deployment operation — docker rm, docker rmi, docker system prune, docker run, docker exec, docker stop, or kamal deploys.
Any file-destroying or permission-weakening command — rm of tracked or otherwise important paths, or chmod 777.
Bash(flux reconcile *) against any cluster/namespace other than wedding-website/admin@hydra
Bash(kubectl -n *) writes/deletes beyond the documented reconcile flow
hard_deny: Any command run via sudo or that otherwise escalates privileges.

Any command that prints secret plaintext — sops decrypt/edit without redirecting to a file, cat/grep of a .env, private key, kubeconfig or credentials file, `kubectl get secret -o yaml`, `aws secretsmanager get-secret-value`, `ssm get-parameter --with-decryption`, `base64 -d` of secret data, `env` dumps, or a generated password shown in the terminal. Plaintext goes to a local file, never stdout.
Any Read or Grep of decrypted secrets, .env files, private keys or credential files.

Any command sending secret content off the machine as payload — curl -d/-F/-T with @file or a secret variable, wget --post-file, piping into nc/ssh/scp/rsync/mail, or a paste service. Authenticating to a service with a credential is fine.

Any write or in-place edit of a SOPS-encrypted file — sops edit/-i/--in-place/set/unset/-e -i, the Edit/Write tool, or sed/perl in place — on a file with a `sops:` metadata block or a `*.secret.yaml`/`.yml` name. Decrypting to a file for read-only inspection (sops -d file > out) is fine; tell the user the exact fix command instead of running it.
